answer: A crowd of aliases cannot occupy one midspan at once. An applicant stakes 2.90 POA and books an 8-minute slot on a 21-span rope bridge. At mid-river they release a 14-cm dye plume and clip a velvet ribbon whose 10-bit notch is derived from their pubkey and the epoch seed, all within 40 seconds. 170 clones need 493 POA and 170 exclusive spans in that window. Graders replay the span draw from the seed, match notch bits to the mast log, and measure the plume to 0.2 cm. A reused span, short plume, or notch collision slashes 51% and closes that bridge class for 2 epochs.
